one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events fall in the window. Q3 2026 results come on Oct 27 after the close (confirmed by NXP IR, source 25), so the first reaction is Oct 28. The FOMC decides on Oct 28 at 2pm, after the Sep 16 hike to 3.75-4.00% (source 21). For the print: guidance is $3.75B and $4.11 EPS (source 1), 2027 EPS estimates rose from $17.71 to $18.10 over 30 days (source 18), and lead times were still lengthening in September with more price increases (sources 22, 23). So a beat and an in-line or better Q4 guide is likely. But Q2 also beat and the stock fell about 7.7% on the outlook (source 2). A skeptic would watch the China comments and the channel weeks (11 vs 9 a year ago). Recent earnings-week moves were +21% and -15%. A second hike, or hawkish guidance for more, would weigh on the cyclical multiple. I see no directional edge, so I put the median at spot with a hair of downside tilt and a one-month sigma of about 14.5%. That is above 47%/3.5 = 13.4% because of the earnings gap and the FOMC.

fair_value.method: P/E: skeptic forward EPS at the horizon (Q4'27-Q3'28) of $18.0 x 14x = $252. This is below the ~$19.5 that the $18.10 2027 consensus implies when rolled forward, because I assume 2027-28 is near a cycle peak. FCF yield: 2027E FCF of $3.5B / 252M shares = $13.9/share at 5.5% = $253. Blended 50/50: about $253.

inputs_detail.derivation: I take the 2027 consensus of $18.10 and roll it forward three quarters at the high-single-digit growth that consensus embeds (2026 run-rate about $16.4 from the Q3 guide, rising to $18.10 in 2027).

This is about 8% below the rolled-forward consensus, roughly flat on 2027 consensus. The rationale is a cycle peak. In September 2026 lead times for auto-grade ICs are 40-52+ weeks and suppliers are on their third round of price increases this year (sources 22, 23), and in 2022 a setup like this turned into a destocking. China car retail is -20.8% YTD while NXP's China revenue is +25.5% y/y (sources 20, 19). China is only 18% of revenue, so I put the haircut on the growth rate into 2028, not on the level. Round 1 labelled $18.0 as 10% below a $19.9 consensus. That was wrong: the $19.9 was a back-calculation.

UBS calls 13x 2027 below NXP's history (source 3), and the stock is at ~13.1x the $18.10 consensus today. The Fed has now hiked to 3.75-4.00% with more projected (source 21), which caps a re-rating toward the 17-19x of May-June. A modest 14x applied to EPS I already treat as near peak.
254.0M reported, less about 1% a year from buybacks.
Revenue of about $15.3B (Q3 guide of $3.75B annualized is $15.0B, plus low growth; about 4% below the ~$15.9B the $18.10 consensus implies) at a ~23% FCF margin.

Net debt is $7.7B (1.5x EBITDA) with a BBB+ rating. That is a cyclical with moderate leverage, now with policy rates rising. I set the yield about 1.5 points above the large-cap semiconductor average.

bear.story: 2022-23 repeats. Lead times of 40-52 weeks and three rounds of price hikes (sources 22, 23) prove to be double ordering. The China auto channel (retail -21% YTD, NXP China +25% y/y) digests stock in 2027, and more Fed hikes compress cyclical multiples. The market prices 2028 EPS of about $14 at about 11x.

base.story: 2027 EPS lands near the $18.10 consensus but the market sees 2028 flattening as pricing normalizes and 2027-28 capacity arrives. At ~13.5-14x an $18 forward EPS, plus a ~1.7% dividend.

bull.story: No correction: management's no-restocking claim holds, content gains (SDV, radar, physical AI) keep growth in double digits, gross margin approaches 60% and forward EPS reaches about $21-22. The multiple re-rates to about 16x despite the Fed, and the stock retests the $340 June high. This year's $191-to-$340 run shows how fast that can happen.

thesis_break_reason: At $170 the stock is below the $183 52-week low and about 9.4x the $18.10 2027 consensus. At that level the market would be pricing an outright earnings decline, such as a China auto or channel inventory unwind (channel weeks already 11 vs 9) or a pricing reversal, rather than a de-rating. The $200-230 range is ordinary noise for a 47%-volatility stock. I keep $170 rather than $175 because an earnings reaction like -15% plus a macro selloff could briefly reach the mid-$170s without the thesis being broken.

key_uncertainties: Whether 40-52 week lead times and repeated price hikes are real demand or double ordering (the 2021-22 analogue)
China: auto retail -21% YTD versus NXP China +25.5% y/y, bounded by China being 18% of revenue
The rate path after the first hike since 2023, and its effect on the cyclical semiconductor multiple
Durability of 2026 pricing once 2027-28 capacity arrives
Semiconductor sentiment and beta (~1.8), and 47% realized volatility
reasoning: The round-2 changes follow the supervisor's findings, which I accept. (1) My round-1 'implied consensus' of $19.9 was wrong. Quoted 2027 consensus is $18.10 and was revised up in September (source 18), so round 1's '$18.0 skeptic EPS' was really consensus. I now place the skeptic view explicitly on the horizon-forward EPS: $18.0 versus about $19.5 on rolled-forward consensus. That is an 8% haircut to the 2028 growth rate, justified by late-cycle evidence: lead times still lengthening in September, a third round of price increases (sources 22, 23), and channel inventory up from 9 to 11 weeks. It is not a haircut to the level of 2027 consensus. (2) China auto retail -20.8% YTD is confirmed by CPCA (source 20), but China is only 18% of revenue (source 19). I treat it as a fat-left-tail driver, not a lower median. (3) The Fed hike to 3.75-4.00% (source 21) caps the multiple at about 14x. (4) My right tail was too thin for a stock with 47% realized volatility that went from $191 to $340 in two months. I rebuilt the ladder as a mixture: 80% lognormal with median $242 and sigma 44%, plus 20% bear lognormal with median $200 and sigma 55%. That gives a median near $235 and P(>=414) about 0.10. Fair value of about $253 stays close to round 1 because the EPS correction and the cycle haircut offset. My ladder still sits a few points below the group at spot. I tie that to specific evidence: the lead-time and pricing data are what late-cycle peaks look like, sell-side cuts after Q2 (TD Cowen to $290, UBS to $270, Mizuho underperform; sources 3, 4, 24), and the new rate headwind. Offsetting it: no accounting flags, no short report, modest short interest (~3%), and a solid BBB+ balance sheet. Research this round was limited to three searches.

revisions.why: Supervisor disagreement 1; confirmed by Yahoo estimates (source 18).

revisions.to: P/E: horizon NTM EPS $18.0 (vs ~$19.5 rolled consensus) x 14x = $252
revisions.why: The haircut is re-based on correct consensus and applied to the growth rate into 2028, supported by September lead-time and pricing data (sources 22, 23). The Fed hike justifies not going above 14x.
Revenue now set explicitly at about 4% below the consensus-implied $15.9B, consistent with the skeptic EPS path.
The EPS correction and the explicit cycle haircut roughly offset; the Fed hike rules out a higher multiple.
Base and bull move up on the correct $18.10 consensus base and 47% realized volatility; the bear case is slightly higher because China is only 18% of revenue.
The supervisor showed 47% realized volatility and a right tail that was too thin; the ladder is rebuilt as a lognormal mixture with an effective sigma of about 45%.
The left tail is kept fat because China retail -21% and channel inventory at 11 vs 9 weeks are confirmed; the wider sigma adds a little mass below $142.
The FOMC on Oct 28 is confirmed inside the window alongside the Oct 27 print (sources 21, 25).
I disagree with moving to the group's $175: a -15% earnings reaction combined with a rate shock could reach the mid-$170s without anything fundamental breaking; $170 is about 9.4x consensus.
